chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a grave whose inhabitant was being punished. Then he passed by it the following year, and behold, he was not being punished. So he said: 'O Lord! I passed by this grave the first year, so he was being punished, and I passed by it this year and he is not being punished.' So Allah revealed to him: 'A righteous son of his has come of age, so he repaired a road and sheltered an orphan, thus for this I have forgiven him for what his son did.'
Then Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The inheritance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His believing servant is a son who worships Him after him.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited the Verse of Zakariyya (peace be upon him): 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself a successor. Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Yaqoub, and make him, my Lord, one with whom You are well pleased.'
ai.seo_question: How can the righteous deeds of a son lead to the forgiveness of his father in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia doctrine of 'Husn al-Khatimah' (good ending) facilitated by the enduring merit of offspring, where a son’s specific acts of charity—such as improving a path or sheltering an orphan—can expiate the father's sins. By linking this to the supplication of Prophet Zakariyya, the Imam emphasizes that a righteous heir serves as a spiritual continuation of the believer's legacy, effectively acting as Allah's 'inheritance' from the deceased. This underscores the practical Islamic principle that familial piety extends beyond biological lineage to encompass moral and spiritual stewardship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu Qurrat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Isa<sup>as</sup> Ibn Maryam<sup>as</sup> passed by a grave whose inhabitant was being Punished. Then he<sup>as</sup> passed by it afterwards so he was not being Punished. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>as</sup> passed by this grave the first year, so he was being Punished, and I<sup>as</sup> passed by it this year and he is not being Punished’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “A righteous son of his became an adult, so he repaired a road, and sheltered an orphan, thus it is due to this I<sup>azwj</sup> Forgave him for what his son had done’.
Then Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(It is) an inheritance of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic from a believing servant to be a son who would worship Him<sup>azwj</sup> from after him’.

Then Abu Abdullahasws recited a Verse of Zakariyyaas [19:5] (Lord) therefore Grant me from Yourself an heir [19:6] Who would inherit me and inherit from the Progeny of Yaqoub, and Make him, my Lord, one with whom You are well Pleased’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from Sharif ibn Sabiq from al-Fadl ibn abu al- Qurrah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said the following: ‘Jesus, son of Marry, once passed by a grave wherein its dweller suffered a great suffering. He passed by the same grave afterward but found the dweller was not suffering. He asked, “O Lord, I passed by this grave a year ago when he was suffering a great suffering and this year I passed by his grave but he did not suffer.” Allah then revealed to him that his virtuous son became mature who repaired a road and gave shelter to an orphan, so I forgave him because of what his son has done.’

The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘It is of the inheritance of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, for His believing servant in the form of a virtuous son who worships Him after the death of his father’
and he (the Imam) then read the verse of the Quran about Zakariya, ‘. . . O Lord, grant me from You an heir who will inherit me and the people of Ya‘qub. O Lord, make him to please You.’”
